Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("81.177.215.15") or RemoteUrl has_any ("")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["81.177.215.15"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic([""]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("81.177.215.15")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("81.177.215.15")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] ARToken/EvilTokens PhaaS infrastructure contact (pamconj.com panel + Cloudflare Worker lure) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Catan and Mouse
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Entra ID device registration = ARToken PRT persistence after device-code token theft · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] ARToken BEC toolkit: inbox forwarding/hiding rule creation on compromised M365 mailbox
ARToken/EvilTokens PhaaS infrastructure contact (pamconj.com panel + Cloudflare Worker lure) AIDelivery High
Hunts endpoint DNS/network connections to the specific ARToken operator-panel and phishing-lure domains published by Talos (dashboard-bl.pamconj.com, spx.pamconj.com, clear90489058903-document.workers.dev). A host resolving/connecting to these means a user reached the device-code phishing lure or operator infrastructure — the earliest on-wire signal of this M365 token-theft campaign. Rationale: Uses the three concrete Talos-published IOC domains plus the pamconj.com apex to catch sibling operator subdomains. These are dedicated malicious infrastructure, so any resolution is high-fidelity; cross-checked against Talos, Sekoia and Microsoft reporting of the same EvilTokens/ARToken infra. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/artoken-inside-an-eviltokens-affiliate-panel-targeting-microsoft-365/ • https://blog.sekoia.io/new-widespread-eviltokens-kit-device-code-phishing-as-a-service-part-1/ • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/04/06/ai-enabled-device-code-phishing-campaign-april-2026/ • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/07/01/eviltokens-device-code-phishing-kit-totally-more-evil-than-we-all-thought/5265409
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1102 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security team detonating the lure URL in a sandbox/SOAR enrichment from a corporate endpoint
  • Threat-intel analyst manually browsing to pamconj.com during investigation
  • Web proxy/URL-scanner appliance pre-fetching the domain for categorization
  • DNS sinkhole or RPZ appliance logging the blocked query (benign but noisy)
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the user/device and confirm whether the connection was a live browser navigation (device-code lure) vs automated scanner; pull the referring email/Teams message for the same recipient. 2) Contain: block all *.pamconj.com and the workers.dev lure at proxy/DNS; if a real user reached the device-code page, revoke that user's refresh tokens/sessions (Revoke-AzureADUserAllRefreshToken) and force re-auth. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2 (new Entra device registration for that user) and UC3 (inbox-rule creation) within 24h; review that user's SigninLogs for device-code grants from unfamiliar IPs.
let ARTokenDomains = dynamic(["dashboard-bl.pamconj.com","spx.pamconj.com","clear90489058903-document.workers.dev","pamconj.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (ARTokenDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let ARTokenDomains = dynamic(["dashboard-bl.pamconj.com","spx.pamconj.com","clear90489058903-document.workers.dev","pamconj.com"]);
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (ARTokenDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, DvcHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Entra ID device registration = ARToken PRT persistence after device-code token theft AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the ARToken/EvilTokens persistence step: after stealing a refresh token via device-code phishing, the operator registers a new device in Entra ID to obtain a Primary Refresh Token for durable SSO that survives password resets. Surfaces device add/register/join audit events with the acting user, source IP and target device for rapid correlation to a suspicious sign-in. Rationale: Grounded in the article's explicit 'Primary Refresh Token (PRT) persistence' capability and corroborated by Sekoia/Microsoft describing refresh-token-driven device registration in Entra ID. Device add/register audit operations are the concrete, queryable footprint of that step; Falcon/CloudWatch left empty because Entra ID audit isn't in FDR or CloudTrail. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/new-widespread-eviltokens-kit-device-code-phishing-as-a-service-part-1/ • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/04/06/ai-enabled-device-code-phishing-campaign-april-2026/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/microsoft-365-phishing-panel-uses-oauth-device-code-flow/
ATT&CKT1098.005 T1528
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate user enrolling a new phone/laptop into Intune/Entra (BYOD or refresh cycle)
  • Autopilot/Intune bulk device provisioning by IT during onboarding
  • Windows Hello for Business device registration on password change
  • Service desk registering a replacement device for a user
Suppression filter
| where ActorIp !in ("<intune_provisioning_egress_ip>")  // NOTE: replace only if you maintain a known Intune egress allowlist; otherwise correlate ActorIp against SigninLogs device-code/foreign-IP sign-ins
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each registration confirm the actor UPN, source IP and device name; check whether the user's most recent sign-in was a device-code grant or came from an unfamiliar/foreign IP within the prior hour. 2) Contain: if unattributable, disable/remove the newly registered device, revoke the user's refresh tokens and PRTs (Revoke-AzureADUserAllRefreshToken + session invalidation), and require MFA re-registration. 3) Hunt: enumerate all devices registered by the same actor IP across the tenant, review SharePoint/OneDrive mass-download and inbox-rule creation (UC3) for the affected mailbox.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("Add registered owner to device","Add registered users to device","Register device","Add device")
| extend Ip = tostring(IPAddress)
| project Timestamp, ActionType, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, Ip, CountryCode, City, ObjectName, ObjectType
| order by Timestamp desc
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where OperationName in ("Add registered owner to device","Add registered users to device","Register device","Add device","Update device")
| extend Actor = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend ActorIp = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| extend TargetDevice = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, Actor, ActorIp, TargetDevice, Result, ResultReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ARToken BEC toolkit: inbox forwarding/hiding rule creation on compromised M365 mailbox AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the ARToken/EvilTokens post-compromise BEC action: automated creation of inbox rules that forward/redirect mail externally and delete or move messages to hide attacker activity. Targets mailbox audit events for New/Set-InboxRule carrying forwarding or delete/move parameters. Rationale: Directly targets ARToken's documented BEC capability ('inbox rule creation for forwarding and deleting messages') via the exact Exchange audit operations and forwarding/delete parameters. Datadog/Falcon/CloudWatch empty because M365 mailbox audit isn't shipped to those platforms in this tenant. Cross-checked against: • https://cyberscoop.com/artoken-bec-platform-cisco-talos/ • https://gbhackers.com/eviltokens-linked-artoken-panel/
ATT&CKT1114.003 T1564.008
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User legitimately setting up out-of-office/auto-forward to a personal or delegate mailbox
  • Admin-configured transport/journaling rule mistaken for a user inbox rule
  • Power-user creating a 'move to folder' organization rule for newsletters
  • Migration tooling recreating rules during a mailbox move
Suppression filter
| where Params !has "@yourcorpdomain.com"  // keep only rules forwarding/redirecting OUTSIDE the org; internal delegate forwarding is common and low-risk
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the rule forwards/redirects to an EXTERNAL domain or deletes/moves security-alert mail; check the ClientIP/country against the user's normal sign-in pattern and recent device-code sign-ins. 2) Contain: delete the malicious rule, revoke the user's tokens and PRTs, reset credentials, and block the external forwarding destination at the mail gateway. 3) Hunt: correlate to UC1 (infra contact) and UC2 (new device registration) for the same user; search for identical rule names/forwarding targets across other mailboxes to scope the BEC blast radius.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","UpdateInboxRules")
| where RawEventData has_any ("ForwardTo","ForwardAsAttachmentTo","RedirectTo","DeleteMessage","MoveToFolder")
| project Timestamp, ActionType, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, CountryCode, ObjectName, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where Operation in ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","UpdateInboxRules")
| extend Params = tostring(Parameters)
| where Params has_any ("ForwardTo","ForwardAsAttachmentTo","RedirectTo","DeleteMessage","MoveToFolder")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Operation, Params, OfficeWorkload
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

union

Unauthenticated write/read to mcp-memory-service /api/documents/* endpoints (CVE-2026-50027) AIExploitation High
Hunts HTTP 200 responses to the unauthenticated document-API routes (upload, batch-upload, search-content, history) on a mcp-memory-service HTTP server, where the request carried no Authorization header. This is the confidentiality/integrity half of the auth-bypass: memory poisoning via upload and stored-content disclosure via search-content/history. Rationale: Anchored on the exact vulnerable route prefixes named at documents.py source lines (upload:149, search-content:729, history) plus HTTP 200; ImWebSession's HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization lets us assert the request was truly unauthenticated, which is the article's core inconsistency (/api/memories 401 vs /api/documents 200). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-84hp-mqvj-3p8h • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/mcp-memory-service/CVE-2026-50027/
ATT&CKT1190 T1213 T1565.001
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Operator deployed the HTTP server WITHOUT MCP_API_KEY/OAuth enabled, so legitimate clients also send no Authorization header
  • Internal ingestion/backup automation that bulk-uploads documents via the same API
  • Vulnerability scanners (Nessus/Nuclei) probing the documented CVE route
  • The operator's own PoC/pen-test traffic against 127.0.0.1
  • Health-check or uptime probes hitting /api/documents/history
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !startswith "127." and SrcIpAddr != "::1"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull all SrcIpAddr hitting /api/documents/* with empty Authorization; confirm the server was launched with MCP_API_KEY/OAuth set (grep env of the memory server --http process). If auth was enabled, every unauthenticated 200 is a real bypass. 2) CONTAIN: Put the service behind the reverse proxy's auth or a WAF rule denying /api/documents/* without a valid bearer, and upgrade mcp-memory-service to >=10.67.1. 3) HUNT: For each attacker IP, correlate preceding /api/memories 401s and following DELETE /api/documents/remove-by-tags; review search-content/{upload_id} responses for exfiltrated memory content and inspect newly uploaded documents for prompt-injection payloads.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Url has "/api/documents/"
| where Url has_any ("/upload", "/batch-upload", "/search-content/", "/history")
| where HttpStatusCode == 200
| where isempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization)   // no API key / OAuth bearer supplied = the CVE-2026-50027 bypass
| where SrcIpAddr !startswith "127."

mcp-memory-service auth-bypass fingerprint: /api/memories 401 then /api/documents 200 from same source AIExploitation High
Correlates the CVE-2026-50027 PoC signature on a single source IP: a 401 on the correctly-protected /api/memories endpoint followed within the hour by a successful (200) request to a /api/documents/* route with no credentials. This two-event shape is far higher fidelity than either request alone because it captures an attacker discovering the inconsistent auth boundary and pivoting to the unprotected router. Rationale: Directly models the PoC attack chain (STEP 1 GET /api/memories -> 401, STEP 4/5 POST/DELETE /api/documents/* -> 200) as a same-source temporal correlation; the 401-then-200 pairing is the article's own proof that the attacker found and exploited the inconsistent auth boundary, making it very low FP. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-84hp-mqvj-3p8h • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/mcp-memory-service/CVE-2026-50027/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A misconfigured legitimate client whose token expired (401 on /api/memories) while a separate unauthenticated automation happens to hit /api/documents from the same NAT egress IP
  • Security scanner walking every route and recording both a 401 and a 200 from one host
  • Shared corporate proxy/NAT collapsing many users behind one SrcIpAddr
  • Operator testing both endpoints during troubleshooting
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the source IP is not a known internal proxy/scanner; inspect the exact /api/documents route that returned 200 (upload = poisoning, search-content = read, remove* = destruction). 2) CONTAIN: Block the source at the WAF/reverse proxy, disable the /api/documents/* router or gate it behind auth, and upgrade to mcp-memory-service >=10.67.1. 3) HUNT: Enumerate every upload_id this IP created or deleted; snapshot current memory store contents, diff against last known-good backup, and purge attacker-injected documents to prevent downstream prompt-injection of the AI agent.
let window = 1h;
let probes = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
    | where Url has "/api/memories" and HttpStatusCode == 401
    | project ProbeTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Url has "/api/documents/" and HttpStatusCode == 200
| where isempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization)
| join kind=inner probes on SrcIpAddr
| where TimeGenerated between (ProbeTime .. ProbeTime + window)
| project ProbeTime, BypassTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod, Url
| order by BypassTime desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/api/memories*" OR Web.url="*/api/documents/*") by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.status, _time span=5m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| eval memories_401=if(like(url,"%/api/memories%") AND status=401, count, 0)
| eval docs_bypass=if(like(url,"%/api/documents/%") AND status=200, count, 0)
| stats sum(memories_401) as memories_401, sum(docs_bypass) as docs_bypass, values(url) as urls, values(dest) as dest, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime by src
| where memories_401 > 0 AND docs_bypass > 0
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/api/memories*" OR Web.url="*/api/documents/*") by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.status, _time span=5m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| eval memories_401=if(like(url,"%/api/memories%") AND status=401, count, 0)
| eval docs_bypass=if(like(url,"%/api/documents/%") AND status=200, count, 0)
| stats sum(memories_401) as memories_401, sum(docs_bypass) as docs_bypass, values(url) as urls, values(dest) as dest, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime by src
| where memories_401 > 0 AND docs_bypass > 0
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
Unauthenticated mass memory deletion via mcp-memory-service DELETE /api/documents/remove-by-tags AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts successful (200) DELETE requests to the unauthenticated /api/documents/remove-by-tags and /api/documents/remove/{upload_id} routes — the availability/integrity impact of CVE-2026-50027 where an attacker permanently destroys memories belonging to authenticated users without credentials. A burst of such DELETEs from one source is a destruction event. Rationale: Uses the specific destructive routes and sink named in the article (remove-by-tags -> storage.delete_by_tags at line 705, remove/{upload_id}) constrained to DELETE + 200; a successful unauthenticated DELETE to these paths is by definition the CVE's availability impact (STEP 5 memories_deleted=1) with essentially no benign equivalent when auth is enabled. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-84hp-mqvj-3p8h • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/mcp-memory-service/CVE-2026-50027/
ATT&CKT1485 T1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin housekeeping that prunes documents by tag through the same API
  • Automated retention/cleanup job deleting expired memories
  • Operator running the published PoC (tag cve-poc) during validation
  • Server started without MCP_API_KEY so all DELETEs are legitimately unauthenticated
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !startswith "127." and SrcIpAddr != "::1"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the DELETEs are unauthenticated (empty Authorization) and the server was configured with auth; count how many upload_ids/tags were removed and from which SrcIpAddr. 2) CONTAIN: Immediately block the source, take the HTTP server offline or gate /api/documents/* behind auth, upgrade to >=10.67.1, and freeze the storage backend for forensic capture before it is overwritten. 3) HUNT: Restore deleted memories from the most recent backup, diff to quantify loss, and pivot on the same IP for prior upload (poisoning) and search-content (exfiltration) calls to scope the full read/write/delete blast radius.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where HttpMethod == "DELETE"
| where Url has_any ("/api/documents/remove-by-tags", "/api/documents/remove/")
| where HttpStatusCode == 200
| where isempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization)
| summarize DeleteCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Urls = make_set(Url, 20) by SrcIpAddr, DstHostname
| order by DeleteCount desc

The Hacker News
2026-07-02 20 use cases 10 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

This week’s security news is mostly about weak spots. Browsers, bots, sandboxes, AI systems, and email flows all show the same problem in different ways. Everything looks normal until someone tests a small gap and finds a way through. This is not one big break. It is small permissions, weak checks, open systems, and normal tools doing things they were allowed to do. That same pattern runs

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] BeepRAT DoH-based C2 resolution + api.service.bio beacon from non-browser process · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains

BeepRAT DoH-based C2 resolution + api.service.bio beacon from non-browser process AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts BeepRAT (customized DCRat) resolving its C2 via DNS-over-HTTPS and beaconing to api.service.bio. Pivots on a non-browser, non-system process reaching public DoH resolver endpoints on 443 and/or the named C2 host, a pattern legitimate apps rarely exhibit. Rationale: Uses the article's named C2 host api.service.bio plus BeepRAT's stated DoH-based C2 resolution behaviour; the domain is paired with behavioural DoH-resolver contact from a non-browser process so the detection does not rest solely on the single-sourced IOC. Cross-checked Rubrik/DCRat lineage via Malpedia. Cross-checked against: • https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.dcrat • https://zerolabs.rubrik.com/
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1573.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Enterprise DoH-enabled agents (some EDR/VPN clients resolve via cloudflare-dns.com)
  • Developer/testing tools that hardcode DoH resolvers
  • Privacy browsers or extensions launched from non-standard binary names
  • Monitoring/uptime agents that health-check public resolvers
  • Legitimate app auto-updaters using 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 DoH
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\", @"\Public\") or RemoteUrl =~ "api.service.bio"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName/FolderPath — flag if HFY.exe or any binary in Downloads/Temp/AppData; pull its SHA256 and check for scheduled-task persistence on the same host. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block api.service.bio at egress/DNS, and kill the offending process tree. 3) Hunt: sweep the org for the same process hash, api.service.bio contact, and schtasks persistence created by the same parent; check for webcam/keylog/screenshot child activity indicative of active BeepRAT tasking.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","svchost.exe","MsMpEng.exe","NisSrv.exe")
| where (RemoteUrl =~ "api.service.bio")
    or (RemotePort == 443 and RemoteUrl in~ ("cloudflare-dns.com","mozilla.cloudflare-dns.com","dns.google","dns.quad9.net","doh.opendns.com","dns.adguard.com","doh.dns.sb"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstPortNumber == 443
| where DstHostname in~ ("api.service.bio","cloudflare-dns.com","mozilla.cloudflare-dns.com","dns.google","dns.quad9.net","doh.opendns.com","dns.adguard.com","doh.dns.sb")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Sessions=count() by SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstHostname, DstIpAddr
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: BeepRAT DoH C2 Resolver Contact From Non-Browser Process
id: 6b1d9c2a-4e7f-4c11-9b7d-2f8a1c0e5d33
description: Detects a non-browser process connecting to public DNS-over-HTTPS resolver endpoints or the BeepRAT C2 host api.service.bio, consistent with DCRat-derived BeepRAT C2 resolution.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/threatsday-ai-compute-hijacking-apple.html
  - https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.dcrat
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/09
tags:
  - attack.t1071.004
  - attack.t1573.001
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationPort: 443
    DestinationHostname:
      - 'api.service.bio'
      - 'cloudflare-dns.com'
      - 'mozilla.cloudflare-dns.com'
      - 'dns.google'
      - 'dns.quad9.net'
      - 'doh.opendns.com'
  filter_browsers:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '\opera.exe'
      - '\iexplore.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_browsers
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(api.service.bio OR cloudflare-dns.com OR mozilla.cloudflare-dns.com OR dns.google OR dns.quad9.net OR doh.opendns.com) -@Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\Chrome.exe OR *\msedge.exe OR *\firefox.exe OR *\Firefox.exe OR *\iexplore.exe OR *\svchost.exe OR *\Svchost.exe)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^(api\.service\.bio|cloudflare-dns\.com|mozilla\.cloudflare-dns\.com|dns\.google|dns\.quad9\.net|doh\.opendns\.com)$/i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera|iexplore|svchost|MsMpEng)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port=443 (All_Traffic.dest="api.service.bio" OR All_Traffic.dest IN ("cloudflare-dns.com","mozilla.cloudflare-dns.com","dns.google","dns.quad9.net","doh.opendns.com","dns.adguard.com","doh.dns.sb")) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.process | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where NOT match(process,"(?i)(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera|iexplore|svchost|MsMpEng)\.exe") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port=443 (All_Traffic.dest="api.service.bio" OR All_Traffic.dest IN ("cloudflare-dns.com","mozilla.cloudflare-dns.com","dns.google","dns.quad9.net","doh.opendns.com","dns.adguard.com","doh.dns.sb")) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.process | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where NOT match(process,"(?i)(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera|iexplore|svchost|MsMpEng)\.exe") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
BeepRAT dropper HFY.exe execution and scheduled-task persistence AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the BeepRAT infection chain where a .NET 'telephone number management' tool HFY.exe runs from a user-writable/archive path and establishes persistence via schtasks. Anchors on the named binary and the article's stated scheduled-task persistence mechanism. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact dropper name HFY.exe (masquerading as a telephone-number tool) and its stated scheduled-task persistence; both the archive-path execution and the schtasks /create spawn are article-specific and high-fidelity. DCRat lineage corroborated via Malpedia. Cross-checked against: • https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.dcrat • https://zerolabs.rubrik.com/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate telecom/CRM utility genuinely named HFY.exe in a corporate app deployment
  • Admin scripting that stages tooling in Public/Temp and registers scheduled tasks
  • Software installers that create scheduled tasks for updaters from AppData
  • Portable apps run from Downloads by power users
  • Security-tool sandboxing that copies binaries to Temp before execution
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("system") and FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files")
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash HFY.exe and detonate/lookup; inspect the created scheduled task's action path and trigger. 2) Contain: disable/delete the malicious scheduled task, quarantine HFY.exe and its bundled DB libraries, isolate host. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same SHA256 org-wide, look for the DoH C2 contact (api.service.bio) and BeepRAT capability artifacts (webcam/keylogger/screenshot, in-memory .NET assembly loads) originating from the same process lineage.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName =~ "HFY.exe" and FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Public\"))
    or (FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/create" and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "HFY.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (TargetProcessName endswith "\\HFY.exe" and TargetProcessName has_any ("\\Downloads\\","\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\","\\Public\\"))
    or (TargetProcessName endswith "\\schtasks.exe" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "/create" and ActingProcessName endswith "\\HFY.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: BeepRAT HFY.exe Execution and Scheduled Task Persistence
id: c4a2f8e1-7b93-4d6a-8f21-9e0b3c7a1d55
description: Detects the BeepRAT dropper HFY.exe running from a user-writable path or spawning schtasks to create persistence, per Rubrik Zero Labs reporting.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/threatsday-ai-compute-hijacking-apple.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/09
tags:
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_dropper:
    Image|endswith: '\HFY.exe'
    Image|contains:
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\'
      - '\Public\'
  selection_persist:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '/create'
    ParentImage|endswith: '\HFY.exe'
  condition: selection_dropper or selection_persist
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\HFY.exe OR *\hfy.exe) AND @Image:(*\Downloads\* OR *\Temp\* OR *\AppData\* OR *\Public\*)) OR (@Image:(*\schtasks.exe OR *\SCHTASKS.EXE) AND @CommandLine:*create* AND @ParentImage:(*\HFY.exe OR *\hfy.exe)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\\HFY\.exe$/i AND ImageFileName=/\\(Downloads|Temp|AppData|Public)\\/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/\/create/i AND ParentBaseFileName=/^HFY\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="HFY.exe" AND (Processes.process_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Public\\*")) OR (Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" AND Processes.process="*/create*" AND Processes.parent_process_name="HFY.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="HFY.exe" AND (Processes.process_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Public\\*")) OR (Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" AND Processes.process="*/create*" AND Processes.parent_process_name="HFY.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Platform-aware phishing: Ninite Loader deploying ConnectWise/Itarian RMM as RAT AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the Cofense-reported Windows payload path where fingerprinted victims receive Ninite Loader which installs ConnectWise ScreenConnect or Itarian RMM abused as a RAT. Pivots on the loader→RMM parent/child chain and RMM binaries launched from user-writable paths. Rationale: Uses the campaign's named tooling — Ninite Loader delivering ConnectWise (ScreenConnect) and Itarian RMM binaries — and the loader→RMM parent/child chain that distinguishes phishing-installed RMM from sanctioned deployment. Corroborated by the Cofense blog and Dark Reading. Cross-checked against: • https://cofense.com/blog/the-platform-you-trust-is-the-platform-they-target • https://www.darkreading.com/application-security/phishing-campaigns-auto-adapt-victims-device-os
ATT&CKT1219 T1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sanctioned MSP/IT deployment of ConnectWise ScreenConnect via Ninite in orgs that use both
  • Legit Itarian/Comodo RMM rollout to endpoints
  • Helpdesk staging RMM installers in Downloads during onboarding
  • Software packaging teams testing Ninite bundles
  • Vendor support session installing ScreenConnect with user consent
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("instance-","screenconnect.com") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the ScreenConnect/Itarian instance is org-sanctioned (check config server/relay URL and code-signing); an unknown relay host = malicious. 2) Contain: block the RMM relay domain/IP at egress, uninstall the unauthorized agent, isolate host, reset the user's credentials. 3) Hunt: review the preceding browser/email chain for the fingerprinting landing page, check other endpoints for the same Ninite parent or RMM relay, and look for macOS/Android users who hit the same lure URL (credential-phish path).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.exe","ITSMAgent.exe","ITSMService.exe","RmmService.exe","rviewer.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Ninite.exe","NiniteOne.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.exe","ITSMAgent.exe","ITSMService.exe","RmmService.exe","rviewer.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("\\Ninite.exe","\\NiniteOne.exe","\\Downloads\\","\\Temp\\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Ninite Loader Spawning ConnectWise or Itarian RMM Abused as RAT
id: a9f3c1b7-2d84-4e5f-9c60-7b1a2e8d4f09
description: Detects Ninite Loader (or a loader from a user-writable path) spawning ConnectWise ScreenConnect or Itarian RMM binaries, per Cofense platform-aware phishing reporting.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/threatsday-ai-compute-hijacking-apple.html
  - https://cofense.com/blog/the-platform-you-trust-is-the-platform-they-target
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/09
tags:
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_rmm:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
      - '\ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe'
      - '\ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.exe'
      - '\ITSMAgent.exe'
      - '\ITSMService.exe'
      - '\RmmService.exe'
      - '\rviewer.exe'
  selection_loader:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\Ninite.exe'
      - '\NiniteOne.exe'
  condition: selection_rmm and selection_loader
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe OR *\ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe OR *\ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.exe OR *\ITSMAgent.exe OR *\ITSMService.exe OR *\RmmService.exe OR *\rviewer.exe) @ParentImage:(*\Ninite.exe OR *\ninite.exe OR *\NiniteOne.exe OR *\Downloads\* OR *\Temp\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(ScreenConnect\.(ClientService|WindowsClient|ClientSetup)|ITSMAgent|ITSMService|RmmService|rviewer)\.exe$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(ninite|niniteone)\.exe$/i OR ParentImageFileName=/\\(Downloads|Temp)\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.exe","ITSMAgent.exe","ITSMService.exe","RmmService.exe","rviewer.exe")) AND (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("Ninite.exe","NiniteOne.exe") OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\Temp\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.exe","ITSMAgent.exe","ITSMService.exe","RmmService.exe","rviewer.exe")) AND (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("Ninite.exe","NiniteOne.exe") OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\Temp\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
INTERPOL law-enforcement lure delivering Proton Drive-hosted password-protected archive AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the Bitdefender-reported campaign of fake law-enforcement 'investigation' emails that pressure recipients into opening a Proton Drive-hosted password-protected archive delivering custom ransomware. Pivots on inbound mail with law-enforcement lure subjects carrying Proton Drive URLs, and on the subsequent archive download. Rationale: Uses the campaign's specific delivery infrastructure (Proton Drive-hosted archive) combined with the article's law-enforcement/'suspicious company activity' lure theme, and the archive extensions of the password-protected payload — far tighter than a generic phishing rule. Corroborated by Bitdefender via the article. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/threatsday-ai-compute-hijacking-apple.html
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate business use of Proton Drive to share zipped files
  • Legal/compliance teams genuinely receiving law-enforcement correspondence with attachments
  • Security researchers downloading zipped samples from Proton Drive
  • Users sharing password-protected archives internally via Proton links
  • Marketing emails using words like 'investigation' or 'evidence' in unrelated context
Suppression filter
| where DeliveryAction == "Delivered" and SenderFromDomain !endswith "proton.me"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the sender is spoofing law enforcement (check SPF/DKIM/DMARC in AuthenticationDetails) and whether the recipient clicked/downloaded the Proton archive. 2) Contain: purge the message org-wide via EmailPostDelivery/soft-delete, block the Proton Drive share URL, and quarantine any downloaded archive on the endpoint. 3) Hunt: if the archive was opened, pivot to DeviceProcessEvents/DeviceFileEvents for archive-spawned execution and mass file-write/rename activity (custom ransomware encryption), and check other recipients of the same sender/subject cluster.
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| join kind=inner (
    EmailUrlInfo
    | where UrlDomain has_any ("drive.proton.me","proton.me","protonmail.com")
    | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| where Subject has_any ("INTERPOL","Investigation","law enforcement","suspicious activity","suspicious company","evidence","police","criminal","prosecutor")
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, SenderDisplayName, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, Url, UrlDomain, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has_any ("drive.proton.me","proton.me")
| where FileName has_any (".zip",".7z",".rar") or tostring(FileMimeType) has_any ("zip","x-7z","rar","octet-stream")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DvcHostname, Url, FileName, FileMimeType, HttpUserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*drive.proton.me*" OR Web.url="*proton.me/urls*" OR Web.url="*proton.me*") (Web.url="*.zip*" OR Web.url="*.7z*" OR Web.url="*.rar*") by Web.src Web.user Web.dest Web.url Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*drive.proton.me*" OR Web.url="*proton.me/urls*" OR Web.url="*proton.me*") (Web.url="*.zip*" OR Web.url="*.7z*" OR Web.url="*.rar*") by Web.src Web.user Web.dest Web.url Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("api.service.bio")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["api.service.bio"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match

NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("api.service.bio")
