ChocoPoC exfiltration upload to 91.132.163.78 AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts ChocoPoC's bulk-exfiltration channel: outbound connections to the campaign's dedicated upload server 91.132.163.78, used for larger stolen-data uploads separate from the Mapbox dead-drop C2. Any host contacting this IP is a confirmed indicator. Rationale: 91.132.163.78 is the article's explicit bulk-upload server, confirmed by The Hacker News and CyberSecurityNews; a hardcoded-IP match is maximally high-fidelity with essentially no legitimate traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/new-chocopoc-rat-targets-vulnerability.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-use-mapbox-dead-drop-c2/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A researcher intentionally connecting to the IP during malware analysis in a sanctioned lab
  • Threat-intel enrichment/scanning tooling actively probing the IOC
  • Shared-egress NAT causing an unrelated host to appear as the source (verify true internal originator)
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process (expect python.exe / gradient loader) and the volume of bytes_out to gauge exfil scope. 2) Contain: block 91.132.163.78 at the firewall/EDR, isolate the host, and preserve netflow/pcap. 3) Hunt: sweep all endpoints for any historical contact with this IP and with api.mapbox.com; on confirmed hosts assume browser creds, SSH keys, and cloud tokens are compromised and rotate them.

| where RemoteIP == "91.132.163.78"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr == "91.132.163.78"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, NetworkBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ChocoPoC Mapbox dead-drop C2 beacon from non-browser process AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts ChocoPoC's covert command channel: a python/non-browser process resolving and calling api.mapbox.com, which the malware abuses as a dead-drop (orders stored in a Mapbox dataset) via DNS-over-HTTPS and domain fronting. Legitimate Mapbox API calls come from mapping apps/browsers, not from python running a cloned PoC. Rationale: Uses the article/CyberSecurityNews-confirmed dead-drop domain (api.mapbox.com) combined with a python/non-browser initiator and clone-path context to separate the C2 abuse from legitimate browser-driven Mapbox traffic. Medium confidence because domain fronting/DoH can mask the true SNI and python geospatial libraries also use Mapbox. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-use-mapbox-dead-drop-c2/ • https://www.sekoia.com/blog/dont-eat-the-chocopocs-how-vulnerability-researchers-were-repeatedly-targeted-by-trojanised-exploits
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Python geospatial/mapping code (folium, geopandas, mapbox SDK) making legitimate Mapbox API calls
  • A researcher's own tooling that renders maps from Mapbox tiles
  • Jupyter/data-science notebooks exported to .py that pull Mapbox basemaps
  • DoH resolver masking the query so only the fronted host is visible (may hide true SNI)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("folium","geopandas","mapbox","contextily","jupyter"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: determine whether the python process is a known geospatial workload or traces to a freshly cloned PoC / gradient.pyd host; inspect the command line and repo path. 2) Contain: if unattributed, isolate the host and block api.mapbox.com egress for that process plus 91.132.163.78. 3) Hunt: correlate the same host/account for the gradient module drop, choco.py execution, browser credential-store reads, and DoH resolver usage; capture the Mapbox dataset ID being polled for IOC sharing.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "mapbox.com"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","python3")
    or (not(InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")) and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", "/tmp/"))
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has "mapbox.com"
| join kind=inner (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","python3")
    | project DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
  ) on DvcHostname
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: |

    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:

        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-64446", "CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2025-14847", "CVE-2026-0257", "CVE-2026-10520", "CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-48908")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Unauthenticated x-ghost-preview request to cached Ghost frontend (CVE-2026-53943 precondition) · [LLM] Ghost x-ghost-preview request carrying XSS payload markers (CVE-2026-53943 execution)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.

Ghost x-ghost-preview cache-poisoning header in inbound HTTP requests (CVE-2026-53943) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for the internal-only x-ghost-preview request header arriving at a Ghost frontend that sits behind a shared cache (Fastly/Cloudflare/nginx proxy_cache). Presence of this header from external/unexpected sources is the precondition for CVE-2026-53943 cache-poisoning XSS, where a preview-altered response gets cached and served to other visitors. Rationale: Uses the exact header token 'x-ghost-preview' named in the advisory as the sole vulnerability trigger; this header is normally emitted only by Ghost's own admin preview flow, so its appearance in shared-cache proxy logs is inherently anomalous. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch left empty — HTTP request headers are not in EDR/CloudTrail schemas. Corroborated against GitLab Advisory DB and DailyCVE (CVSS 9.6). Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/ghost/CVE-2026-53943/ • https://dailycve.com/ghost-cms-cache-poisoning-xss-cve-2026-53943-critical-dc-jul2026-821/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Ghost editor/author using the built-in post-preview feature
  • Shared preview links opened by reviewers or marketing staff
  • CMS integration or headless-build job pre-rendering preview content
  • Synthetic monitoring / uptime checks configured to hit preview URLs
  • Internal QA automation validating draft rendering
Suppression filter
| where isempty(RequestCookies) or RequestCookies !has "ghost"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the source IP(s) and confirm whether they belong to known editorial staff, CI/build systems, or monitoring. Check whether the same request also carried a valid Ghost session cookie (legit) or none (suspicious). 2) Contain: at the cache layer (Fastly/Cloudflare/nginx) add the documented workaround — bypass/vary cache for any request carrying x-ghost-preview — and confirm Ghost is upgraded to >=6.37.0. 3) Hunt: for each poisoned URL, check whether subsequent cache-HIT responses were served to other clients, and review admin/staff logons on the frontend domain for account takeover.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Message has "x-ghost-preview" or RequestContext has "x-ghost-preview"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Ghost x-ghost-preview Cache-Poisoning Header (CVE-2026-53943)
id: 3f6c1e2a-9b4d-4c7e-8a11-2d5f7c9e4a10
status: experimental
description: Detects the internal-only x-ghost-preview request header at a Ghost frontend behind a shared cache, the precondition for CVE-2026-53943 cache-poisoning XSS.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-62q6-4hv4-vjrw
  - https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/ghost/CVE-2026-53943/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/08
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  keywords:
    - 'x-ghost-preview'
  condition: keywords
level: medium
source:linux.syslog "x-ghost-preview"
CLOUD
index=web OR index=proxy (sourcetype="nginx:plus:access" OR sourcetype="nginx:access" OR sourcetype="access_combined" OR sourcetype="cloudflare:json" OR sourcetype="fastly") "x-ghost-preview"
| stats count as hits, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(uri_path) as uri_path, dc(clientip) as distinct_clients by host, sourcetype, clientip
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - hits
Unauthenticated x-ghost-preview request to cached Ghost frontend (CVE-2026-53943 precondition) AIExploitation High
Alerts when the x-ghost-preview header arrives with no session cookie present — the exact unauthenticated-attacker precondition the advisory calls out. Legitimate preview traffic carries a Ghost staff session; an anonymous request setting this header is an exploitation attempt against the shared cache. Rationale: Combines the advisory's exact header token with its stated precondition ('an unauthenticated user could send an x-ghost-preview header') by requiring absence of any Ghost session cookie, which cleanly separates malicious anonymous abuse from legit authenticated preview. Datadog/Sigma omitted — reliable cookie-absence negation is not expressible on free-text syslog or single-selection Sigma. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch omitted (no HTTP header telemetry). Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/ghost/CVE-2026-53943/ • https://dailycve.com/ghost-cms-cache-poisoning-xss-cve-2026-53943-critical-dc-jul2026-821/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized penetration test or bug-bounty researcher probing the CVE
  • CDN misconfiguration that strips cookies before logging
  • Internal QA script deliberately exercising preview without login
  • Anonymized/privacy-proxy traffic that removes cookie headers before the WAF
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the request had no valid Ghost staff session and identify the source IP/ASN and the targeted URL. A single anonymous host repeatedly setting x-ghost-preview across multiple URLs is high-confidence exploitation. 2) Contain: apply the cache-layer workaround (bypass cache on x-ghost-preview) immediately, block the offending source at the WAF, and confirm/schedule upgrade to Ghost >=6.37.0. 3) Hunt: enumerate every URL this source touched, check the cache for poisoned entries, and review staff-account activity on the frontend domain; if credential compromise is suspected use Ghost's 'Reset all authentication' (>=6.41.0).
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Message has "x-ghost-preview" or RequestContext has "x-ghost-preview"
| where isempty(RequestCookies) or RequestCookies !has "ghost"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestCookies, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
index=web OR index=proxy (sourcetype="nginx:plus:access" OR sourcetype="nginx:access" OR sourcetype="access_combined" OR sourcetype="cloudflare:json" OR sourcetype="fastly") "x-ghost-preview"
| search NOT _raw="*Cookie:*" AND NOT _raw="*ghost-admin-api-session*"
| stats count as hits, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(uri_path) as uri_path by host, clientip
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - hits
Ghost x-ghost-preview request carrying XSS payload markers (CVE-2026-53943 execution) AIExploitation High
Alerts when an x-ghost-preview request also contains HTML/JavaScript injection markers — the actual XSS payload that CVE-2026-53943 renders into the frontend response and stores in the shared cache to be served to subsequent visitors. Pairs the vulnerability trigger with the malicious content in one event. Rationale: Correlates the advisory's exact vulnerability trigger (x-ghost-preview) with classic reflected/stored XSS markers in the same request, capturing the injected content that gets rendered and cached ('served to subsequent visitors'). Very low FP because a preview request AND a script payload together has no benign explanation. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch omitted — no HTTP payload telemetry in those sources. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/ghost/CVE-2026-53943/ • https://dailycve.com/ghost-cms-cache-poisoning-xss-cve-2026-53943-critical-dc-jul2026-821/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Automated web vulnerability scanner (Burp/Acunetix/Nuclei) firing XSS probes with the preview header
  • Authorized penetration test validating CVE-2026-53943
  • WAF already blocked the request but still logged it (check DeviceAction/Activity)
  • Legitimate blog content whose title/body genuinely contains the literal string '<script' in a code sample
Suppression filter
| where DeviceAction != "blocked" and DeviceAction != "deny"
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the injected payload from the request and the target URL; confirm whether the WAF blocked or passed it, and whether the response was subsequently cached and served (cache HIT) to other clients. 2) Contain: purge the affected URL(s) from the shared cache, apply the x-ghost-preview cache-bypass workaround, block the source IP, and verify Ghost is >=6.37.0. 3) Hunt: search staff logons on the frontend domain and any admin-session cookies for signs of takeover, review all URLs the source touched, and if compromise is confirmed invoke Ghost 'Reset all authentication' (>=6.41.0).
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Message has "x-ghost-preview" or RequestContext has "x-ghost-preview"
| where Message has_any ("<script", "onerror=", "onload=", "javascript:", "<svg", "<img", "%3Cscript", "document.cookie")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Ghost x-ghost-preview Request With XSS Payload (CVE-2026-53943)
id: 8b21d4f7-6e3a-4d92-b0c5-1a7e9f3c2b44
status: experimental
description: Detects an x-ghost-preview request that also carries HTML/JavaScript injection markers, the CVE-2026-53943 cache-poisoning XSS payload.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-62q6-4hv4-vjrw
  - https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/ghost/CVE-2026-53943/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/08
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  sel_header:
    - 'x-ghost-preview'
  sel_payload:
    - '<script'
    - 'onerror='
    - 'onload='
    - 'javascript:'
    - '<svg'
    - '%3Cscript'
    - 'document.cookie'
  condition: sel_header and sel_payload
level: high
source:linux.syslog "x-ghost-preview" AND ("<script" OR "onerror=" OR "javascript:" OR "<svg" OR "document.cookie")
WEB
index=web OR index=proxy (sourcetype="nginx:plus:access" OR sourcetype="nginx:access" OR sourcetype="access_combined" OR sourcetype="cloudflare:json" OR sourcetype="fastly") "x-ghost-preview"
| search _raw="*<script*" OR _raw="*onerror=*" OR _raw="*onload=*" OR _raw="*javascript:*" OR _raw="*<svg*" OR _raw="*%3Cscript*" OR _raw="*document.cookie*"
| stats count as hits, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(uri_path) as uri_path by host, clientip
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - hits
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-53943")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-53943")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-53943")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-53943")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity

Rancher Manager assets vulnerable to CVE-2026-41052 (PSA privilege-escalation exposure) AIReconnaissance High
Vulnerability-exposure hunt surfacing hosts running Rancher Manager versions affected by CVE-2026-41052 (< 2.12.10, < 2.13.6, < 2.14.2) so the SOC can prioritise patching or applying the project-owner role workaround. Article-specific via the exact CVE ID and patched-version boundaries. Rationale: Direct CveId match against the TVM vulnerability inventory using the article's CVE and the patched-version boundaries (2.12.10 / 2.13.6 / 2.14.2) confirmed by NVD and the v2.14.2 release notes. Pure exposure hunt, minimal FP. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-41052 • https://github.com/rancher/rancher/releases/tag/v2.14.2
ATT&CKT1190 T1068
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Rancher instance already patched but TVM inventory not yet refreshed (stale scan)
  • Air-gapped/isolated Rancher not exploitable from the untrusted network but still flagged
  • Rancher server node where TVM detects the binary but the project-owner role has already been custom-hardened per the workaround
  • Version string mismatch where a backported vendor build carries the fix without a version bump
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the detected SoftwareVersion is truly below 2.12.10 / 2.13.6 / 2.14.2 and identify who has Cluster Member / Project Owner access on that instance. 2) Contain: schedule upgrade to a patched release, or immediately apply the workaround — replace the wildcard on the project-owner role with the explicit verbs get/update/delete/patch/create/list/watch/deletecollection to strip updatepsa. 3) Hunt: on flagged instances, run the PSA-label-downgrade and project-owner-binding UCs over the last 30 days to check for prior exploitation.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Fleet valuesFrom cross-namespace secret/configmap reference (CVE-2026-44935) · [LLM] Fleet agent service account reads secrets across multiple namespaces (CVE-2026-44935)
Fleet valuesFrom cross-namespace secret/configmap reference (CVE-2026-44935) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts Rancher Fleet GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle custom resources whose spec contains a `valuesFrom` block with a secretKeyRef/configMapKeyRef, the exact mechanism CVE-2026-44935 abuses to read secrets in namespaces the tenant is not authorized for. Article-specific because it pivots on the Fleet CRD resource names plus the `valuesFrom` key-reference structure rather than generic secret access. Rationale: Uses the exact Fleet CRD resource names (gitrepos/helmops/bundles from go:github.com/rancher/fleet) and the `valuesFrom` + secretKeyRef/configMapKeyRef structure named in GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x as the exploitation vector; high-fidelity because legitimate fleet.yaml normally references secrets in the same namespace only. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/007/
ATT&CKT1552.007
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate multi-namespace GitOps deployment where an operator intentionally references a shared config namespace
  • Fleet platform team testing valuesFrom against a sanctioned central secrets namespace
  • CI pipelines that template Bundles with valuesFrom to a common values ConfigMap
  • Upgrade migrations that recreate existing GitRepo resources with unchanged valuesFrom blocks
Suppression filter
| where not (Username has "system:serviceaccount:cattle-fleet-system" and ObjNamespace == extract(@"namespace:\s*([a-z0-9-]+)", 1, ReqStr))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full RequestObject; compare the namespace inside valuesFrom to ObjectRef.namespace and to the tenant that owns the requesting Username — a mismatch to a namespace the tenant has no RBAC in is the true positive. 2) Contain: delete/suspend the offending GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle, and rotate any secret whose name/namespace/key appears in the valuesFrom reference (advisory explicitly recommends rotation). 3) Hunt: enumerate all Fleet CRs created by the same Username across the cluster and check whether the Fleet agent service account subsequently read those referenced secrets (see companion fan-out UC).
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Verb in ("create","update","patch")
| extend ObjResource = tostring(ObjectRef.resource), ObjNamespace = tostring(ObjectRef.namespace)
| where ObjResource in ("gitrepos","helmops","bundles")
| extend ReqStr = tostring(RequestObject)
| where ReqStr has "valuesFrom" and (ReqStr has "secretKeyRef" or ReqStr has "configMapKeyRef")
| where ReqStr has "namespace"    // cross-namespace ref requires an explicit namespace inside valuesFrom
| project TimeGenerated, Username, Verb, ObjResource, ObjNamespace, RequestUri, ReqStr
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Rancher Fleet valuesFrom Cross-Namespace Secret Reference (CVE-2026-44935)
id: b3f1c8a2-7d4e-4a1b-9c2f-6e8a5d3b1f04
description: Detects Fleet GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle resources whose spec embeds a valuesFrom secretKeyRef/configMapKeyRef, the vector for CVE-2026-44935 cross-namespace secret disclosure.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/07
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.007
logsource:
  product: kubernetes
  service: audit
detection:
  selection_verb:
    verb:
      - create
      - update
      - patch
  selection_resource:
    objectRef.resource:
      - gitrepos
      - helmops
      - bundles
  selection_valuesfrom:
    requestObject|contains: 'valuesFrom'
  selection_keyref:
    requestObject|contains:
      - 'secretKeyRef'
      - 'configMapKeyRef'
  condition: selection_verb and selection_resource and selection_valuesfrom and selection_keyref
level: high
source:kubernetes.audit @verb:(create OR update OR patch) @objectRef.resource:(gitrepos OR helmops OR bundles) valuesFrom (secretKeyRef OR configMapKeyRef)
CLOUD
index=kube_audit (verb=create OR verb=update OR verb=patch) ("objectRef.resource"=gitrepos OR "objectRef.resource"=helmops OR "objectRef.resource"=bundles) requestObject=*valuesFrom* (requestObject=*secretKeyRef* OR requestObject=*configMapKeyRef*) | table _time, user.username, verb, objectRef.resource, objectRef.namespace, requestURI | sort - _time
Fleet agent service account reads secrets across multiple namespaces (CVE-2026-44935) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the downstream-cluster fingerprint of CVE-2026-44935: the Fleet agent service account issuing get/list of secrets or configmaps across an abnormal number of distinct namespaces within a short window, indicating cross-tenant credential harvesting via unrestricted valuesFrom/HelmOp deployment. Article-specific because it keys on the Fleet agent SA identity and the cross-namespace fan-out the advisory tells defenders to review logs for. Rationale: Pivots on the Fleet agent service account identity (cattle-fleet-system fleet-agent) reading secrets/configmaps across namespaces — the exact post-exploit behaviour GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x tells operators to review cluster logs for and to drive credential rotation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/007/
ATT&CKT1552.007 T1613
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate multi-tenant cluster where the Fleet agent SA is authorized to deploy into many namespaces by design
  • Initial Fleet onboarding/bootstrap that syncs bundles into a large set of namespaces at once
  • Backup/DR tooling running under a fleet-labelled SA enumerating secrets
  • Cluster-wide chart rollout (e.g. cert-manager, monitoring) driven through Fleet touching every namespace
Response runbook
1) Triage: list the distinct namespaces and secret names the Fleet agent SA touched; confirm against the tenant boundary — reads into namespaces owned by a different tenant are the true positive. 2) Contain: rotate the Fleet agent service account token and every secret it read cross-tenant, then apply the patched-version Policy resource pinning a least-privilege service account per GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle namespace. 3) Hunt: correlate back to companion UC (valuesFrom cross-namespace references) to identify which GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle CR triggered the reads and which tenant Username authored it; upgrade Fleet to v0.15.2/v0.14.6/0.13.11/v0.12.15.
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where Verb in ("get","list","watch")
| extend Resource = tostring(ObjectRef.resource), NS = tostring(ObjectRef.namespace)
| where Resource in ("secrets","configmaps")
| where Username has "serviceaccount" and Username has "fleet"
| summarize NamespaceCount = dcount(NS), Namespaces = make_set(NS, 50), Requests = count() by Username, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where NamespaceCount > 3    // 3 = a single Fleet agent normally serves a bounded tenant namespace set; fan-out beyond that is the CVE signal
| order by NamespaceCount desc
source:kubernetes.audit @verb:(get OR list OR watch) @objectRef.resource:(secrets OR configmaps) @user.username:*fleet*
CLOUD
index=kube_audit (verb=get OR verb=list OR verb=watch) ("objectRef.resource"=secrets OR "objectRef.resource"=configmaps) "user.username"=*fleet* | stats dc(objectRef.namespace) AS NamespaceCount values(objectRef.namespace) AS Namespaces count AS Requests by user.username | where NamespaceCount > 3 | sort - NamespaceCount
